report.tagline: The world's biggest video app, where anyone can upload and creators earn a share of the ad and subscription money their videos bring in.
report.simpleSummary: YouTube is a free video app where you can watch almost anything: cooking, cricket highlights, music, coding tutorials, or a 30-second Short. Most videos are made by ordinary creators, not TV studios. YouTube shows ads and gives creators a share of the money. If you hate ads, you can pay for YouTube Premium.

overview.whatItDoes: YouTube hosts billions of videos uploaded by creators, from long videos and live streams to Shorts and podcasts. Viewers watch free with ads or pay for Premium. Advertisers pay to show ads, and YouTube splits ad money with creators in its Partner Program.
howItWorks: Creators upload videos, Shorts, live streams or podcasts for free.
YouTube's recommendation system picks what each viewer sees on Home, Up Next and the Shorts feed.
Advertisers bid through Google Ads for ads before, during and between videos.
Creators in the YouTube Partner Program get about 55% of ad money on long videos and 45% on Shorts.
Viewers can pay for Premium (no ads, background play, downloads) or channel memberships and Super Chats.
YouTube TV, a US live TV bundle, and NFL Sunday Ticket sell paid sports and channels.
overview.valueProposition: For viewers: almost any video you want, free, on any screen. For creators: a huge audience and a share of the money. For advertisers: the biggest video audience in the world, now mostly watching on TV screens too.

painPoints.howSolved: Free tutorials on almost any topic, in many languages.

painPoints.pain: Cable TV is expensive and rigid.
painPoints.howSolved: Free YouTube on smart TVs, plus YouTube TV and Primetime Channels for paid TV.

painPoints.pain: Creators need an audience and a way to earn without a studio.
painPoints.howSolved: Anyone can upload, and the Partner Program shares ad money.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Picks videos for each viewer based on watch history and satisfaction surveys.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Drives most watch time, which drives ad money.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Vertical short videos up to 3 minutes in a swipe feed.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Competes with TikTok and Reels and brings in young viewers and new creators.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shares ad and Premium money with creators who meet entry rules.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Keeps the best creators on YouTube, which keeps viewers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Ad-free videos, background play, downloads and YouTube Music.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: A big subscription business that does not depend on advertisers.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: YouTube on smart TVs, with a lean-back interface and podcasts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: TV is where YouTube is growing fastest and where ads pay the most.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Matches uploads with copyrighted music and video so owners can block or earn from them.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Lets YouTube host huge amounts of music legally and keeps rights holders happy.

steps.detail: Types 'DSA linked list in Hindi' on YouTube or Google.
Chooses based on thumbnail, views and length.
Watches a 5-second skippable ad from an ed-tech company.
Saves the playlist and subscribes to the channel.
Home feed now shows the next videos in the series.
Comes back to continue the playlist.
Posts two videos and several Shorts a week.
Hits 1,000 subscribers and 4,000 watch hours (or 10 million Shorts views in 90 days).
Links an AdSense account and gets reviewed.
Ads start running; earnings show in YouTube Studio.
Turns on memberships, Super Thanks and shopping links.
Earnings above the payment threshold are paid to the bank.
Music stops when the phone screen locks.
Gets a one-month free Premium trial prompt.
Uses background play and downloads on the commute.
Builds playlists from songs watched as videos.
Trial ends and the monthly fee starts.
Keeps paying if ad-free feels worth it, or switches to Lite.

businessModel.summary: YouTube makes money from ads first, and from subscriptions second. Advertisers paid $11.2 billion in Q3 2026 alone. Subscriptions like Premium, Music, YouTube TV and NFL Sunday Ticket are growing fast. YouTube pays a big share of this money to creators and music labels.

revenueStreams.detail: Ads on videos, Shorts and TV, sold through Google Ads. $11.2 billion in Q3 2026, about $40 billion or more a year.
150 million or more subscribers paying monthly fees, with money shared with creators and labels.

revenueStreams.stream: YouTube TV and NFL Sunday Ticket
revenueStreams.detail: US live TV bundle and NFL games package, sold by subscription.
YouTube takes a cut of channel memberships, Super Chats and shopping commissions.

businessModel.pricing: Free with ads. YouTube Premium is about ₹149 a month for one person in India and about $13.99 in the US; Premium Lite (fewer ads, no music) is cheaper in some countries. YouTube TV is about $83 a month in the US. Prices vary by country and plan.
costDrivers: Payouts to creators (about 55% of long-form ad money)
Royalties to music labels and publishers
Sports and TV rights like NFL Sunday Ticket
Video storage, data centres and bandwidth
Content moderation and trust and safety teams
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take $1,000 of ads on long videos. About $550 goes to the creator, and YouTube keeps about $450 to pay for servers, bandwidth and staff. On Shorts, YouTube keeps more, 55%, but Shorts ads earn much less per view. A US viewer on a TV is worth far more than a phone viewer in India, because TV ads sell at a higher price. A Premium subscriber paying ₹149 in India brings steady money, but most of it is shared with creators and labels.

howTheyGetUsers: Google Search results that show YouTube videos
Links shared on WhatsApp, X and other apps
Pre-installed on every Android phone and most smart TVs
whatBringsUsersBack: Subscriptions to favourite creators and notifications for new videos
Personalised Home feed and endless Shorts feed
Live events like cricket highlights, music launches and podcasts
Playlists and watch history across phone and TV
growth.moat: YouTube has the most creators and the most viewers, and each side keeps the other there. Creators go where the audience and money are, and viewers go where the creators are. Add Google's ad system, Content ID with music labels, and 20 years of watch data, and it is very hard to copy.

northStar.metric: Satisfied watch time: hours watched where viewers rate the video as worth their time
northStar.why: This north star metric rewards videos people value, not just clickbait. More satisfied time means more ad views and more reason to pay for Premium.

guardrailMetrics: Premium cancellation rate after price changes
strengths: Largest video audience and creator base in the world
Number one on US TV screens with over 15% of viewing time
Two strong money engines: ads and over 150 million subscriptions
Google's ad system and search traffic behind it
weaknesses: Ad growth slowed to about 9% in Q3 2026
Shorts earn much less per view than long videos
Heavy dependence on unpaid moderation by AI and on creator goodwill
Kids and harmful content problems bring repeated criticism
risks: TikTok and Reels competing for young viewers' time
Regulation on kids' safety, ads and competition, especially against Google
Creator anger over tougher Partner Program rules from 2027
userComplaints: More and longer ads, including unskippable ones on TV
Crackdown on ad blockers that breaks playback
Recommendations full of clickbait or repeated videos
Creators complain about demonetisation, copyright strikes and doubled entry rules for the Partner Program

improvementIdeas.idea: Let viewers on TV pick 'one longer ad break now' instead of several mid-roll ads.
improvementIdeas.problem: Viewers hate frequent unskippable ads on TV.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Higher satisfaction with similar ad revenue.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Watch time per TV session and ad revenue per hour

improvementIdeas.idea: Price Premium Lite in India below ₹89 for ad-light viewing without music.
improvementIdeas.problem: Many Indian users find ₹149 too high but dislike ads.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More paying users in price-sensitive markets.

improvementIdeas.idea: Clear demonetisation reasons with timestamps and a one-click fix and re-review.
improvementIdeas.problem: Creators lose income without knowing why.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Less creator anger and faster fixes.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Appeal resolution time and creator satisfaction

improvementIdeas.idea: 'Hide AI-made Shorts' setting, using existing AI labels.
improvementIdeas.problem: Viewers complain about low-quality AI videos.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better satisfaction in the Shorts feed.

improvementIdeas.idea: New creator starter fund in Shorts for creators below the new 2027 entry bar.
improvementIdeas.problem: Tougher rules may push new creators to TikTok.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: New channels uploading weekly after 90 days

pmLessons: Two-sided platforms win by keeping both sides happy. YouTube's creator revenue share is why the best creators stay.
Follow the screen. YouTube grew by moving from phones and laptops to TVs, where ads earn more.
Measure satisfaction, not just time. Watch time alone rewards clickbait, so YouTube asks viewers what they valued.
A free product can still build a big subscription business if it gives a clear reason to pay, like no ads.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow YouTube Premium subscribers in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users (music listeners, students, families). Look at price, value, and payment like UPI autopay. Propose a test and metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: Shorts views are huge but earn little. How would you improve Shorts monetisation?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split into views, ad load, ad price and creator payouts. Consider shopping, brand deals and moving viewers to long-form.

interviewQuestions.question: What metric would you use to judge YouTube's recommendation system?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare watch time vs satisfied watch time. Add guardrails for harmful content and creator diversity.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a YouTube feature for families watching on TV.
interviewQuestions.hint: Define the users (parents, kids). Find pains: shared profiles, kids' safety, picking content together. Propose a feature and success metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: YouTube is raising the bar for creators to earn. How would you evaluate this decision?
interviewQuestions.hint: Consider quality, spam, payouts and creator supply. Model winners and losers and set metrics to watch.
